title: DataFrames -- read, transform, write
exp: The DataFrame API deliberately mirrors SQL and pandas. Key differences: laziness, Parquet output, and explicit schema for production.
pts: spark.read.csv(path, header=True, inferSchema=True) -- inferSchema samples file to guess types (slow on large files in production).
Explicit StructType schema: faster and safer for production pipelines.
df.coalesce(4) before write -- reduces small file count without a full shuffle.
code:
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, when, to_date
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, IntegerType, DoubleType, StringType

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName('Pipeline').getOrCreate()

schema = StructType([
    StructField('order_id', IntegerType(), False),
    StructField('amount',   DoubleType(),  True),
    StructField('status',   StringType(),  True),
])
df = spark.read.csv('s3://bucket/orders/', header=True, schema=schema)

df_clean = (df
    .filter(col('amount').isNotNull() & (col('amount') > 0))
    .withColumn('tier',
        when(col('amount') > 10000, 'platinum')
        .when(col('amount') > 1000, 'gold')
        .otherwise('standard'))
    .dropDuplicates(['order_id'])
    .na.fill({'status': 'unknown'}))

df_clean.coalesce(4).write.mode('overwrite').parquet('s3://bucket/processed/')

qa.q: Why write Parquet instead of CSV?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Parquet is columnar -- analytical queries reading only a few columns read only those from disk. CSV reads entire rows. Parquet also compresses effectively, stores schema (no type inference needed), and supports partition pruning. Typically 10-100x faster to read than CSV for analytics queries.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Python interpreter executes bytecode under the CPython Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), managing objects via reference counting and cycle GC.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Attempting CPU-bound parallelism with Python threading fails due to GIL serialization; memory leaks occur from circular references.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Multiprocessing bypasses the GIL for CPU tasks at the cost of inter-process communication (IPC) serialization overhead.

**Elevator Pitch:** Spark creates one file per partition. With 200 partitions you get 200 small files. Reading 200 small S3 files is much slower than 4-10 larger ones due to per-file overhead. Fix: df.coalesce(4) before writing -- merges partitions without a full shuffle. repartition(4) also works but triggers a full shuffle.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Spark Driver compiles DataFrame operations into a Catalyst logical plan, optimizes it into a Physical plan, and distributes tasks across Executor JVMs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Data skew on join/group keys forces single executors to spill to disk or fail with OutOfMemory (OOM) errors.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Broadcasting small tables eliminates expensive network shuffles, but broadcasting large tables exhausts Driver memory.
